newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM resigned to finance minister going.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM resigned to finance minister going.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Friday he would have to accept Finance Minister Aivar Kreituss would leave his post after Kreituss was dismissed from his own party, and thus had no party allegiance.
Shkele said two weeks had elapsed since Kreituss had been dismissed and that under the government coalition rules he had to join another party or leave the government.
"There cannot be a minister in this government for whom no party takes responsibility," Shkele told a news conference.
"I will have to take this decison (accept Kreituss' departure)," he added.
Kreituss was dismissed from his Democratic Party Saimnieks (DPS), the largest party in the six-group coalition, amid internal rivalries with the party leadership.
He was criticised for failing to implement party policy as finance minister although Kreituss said his job was to follow government policy.
Shkele said the 1997 budget, which has started going through parliament, would not be threatened by Kreituss' departure and that he would probably guide it through parliament himself.
Two state finance ministers will also have to resign. The new finance minister will again be nominated by the DPS.
